subject: AWS Marketplace listing ratecard redesign — renewal options and playbook
messages:
From: Alicia Chen <alicia.chen@amazon.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: AWS Marketplace renewal & ratecard template

Aditya,

Thanks again for the productive sync last week. Procurement and partner ops have asked us to revisit the listing economics ahead of your May renewal window so we can align on the next term and placement in the Marketplace catalog. We're seeing strong demand signals for your product and want to make sure the commercial framework reflects the new GTM work (co-sell, webinars, sponsored listings).

Attached is the standard AWS marketplace ratecard template (we typically ask partners to propose a preferred structure):
- Option A: Revenue share (standard % bands based on net revenue)
- Option B: Flat annual listing fee + variable marketing credits
- Option C: Tiered blended model (lower rev-share for committed volume + listing fee)

Can you share Redwood's preferred design and any internal guardrails (min ARR, target margin, absolute floor for rev-share)? Procurement will need a short memo + usage history to model P&L. If helpful, I can loop in aws-procurement@amazon.com to establish a paper trail for finance.

Would next Thursday, May 6 at 10am PT work for a 30-minute ratecard workshop?

Best,
Alicia Chen
Senior Partner Manager, AWS Marketplace
Alicia.Chen@amazon.com

Attachment: aws_ratecard_template.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Alicia Chen <alicia.chen@amazon.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-25T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace renewal & ratecard template

Alicia — thanks for the note and template. Looping in Laura (Finance) and Marissa (Head of Partnerships) to review the numbers and guardrails. Initial thoughts from my side:

- We prefer a blended approach (Option C) so we get predictable dollars for GTM while preserving upside on higher revenue.
- Target band: aim for 12–15% effective rev-share at current volumes, with a $100k annual listing fee to secure co-marketing slots.
- If procurement pushes hard on pure rev-share, we should counter with a tier that drops rev-share to ~8% at >$2M ARR to stimulate scale.

I attached a short usage export and our Q1 revenue by channel to help model. Please confirm if AWS prefers a single final document or a short two-page memo + template.

I can do May 6 at 10am PT. Adding that to the calendar once we confirm attendees.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive — Strategic Partners
Redwood Inference

Attachment: usage_summary_Q1_2027.csv (CSV)
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-26T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace renewal & ratecard template

Quick internal notes:

- Finance preference: favor a predictable minimum (listing fee) so we can underwrite co-marketing commitments. We can trade some margin to get guaranteed marketing slots.
- Legal: we'll need a short SOW that ties any marketing commitments to measurable deliverables (impressions, leads). Ask Partnerships to draft KPIs.
- Procurement risk: if they insist on high rev-share, we should insist on term >9 months and a step-down schedule.

Karthik, can you pull historic co-sell contribution metrics? Even a one-slide summary will help procurement model uplift.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Finance (Revenue Ops)
Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-26T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace renewal & ratecard template

On it — attaching a quick snapshot (pasted below) and will add to the playbook:

- Co-sell pipeline influenced via AWS: $420k in closed ARR last 12 months
- Webinar-generated leads (with AWS promos): 310 MQLs, ~18% SQL conversion
- Average deal size from marketplace-led trial: $48k

If we push for marketing credits, we should ask for placement guarantees for the first 3 months after renewal — that's when lift is highest.

-Karthik
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Alicia Chen <alicia.chen@amazon.com>, aws-procurement@amazon.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-02T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood proposed ratecard + playbook for May renewal workshop

Alicia / procurement — thanks for the template. Per our internal review, attached is Redwood's proposed ratecard (proposed_ratecard_v2.xlsx) and a 2-page playbook (redwood_aws_listing_playbook.pdf) that lays out the ask and how we measure success. Summary of our proposal:

- Term: 9 months (auto-renew) with a 90-day review clause
- Commercial structure: Blended (preferred) — $100,000 flat annual listing fee + tiered rev-share: 14% up to $500k ARR, 10% between $500k–$2M, 8% >$2M
- Marketing: $150,000 commit in AWS credits (or equivalent co-marketing spend) tied to a 3-month placement guarantee post-launch
- Deliverables: joint webinar (1), one sponsored blog post, homepage placement in Marketplace for 30 days on launch

If procurement prefers to exclude a listing fee, our fallback is a pure rev-share with a higher first-year floor (15% blended) and deeper volume tier drop. We are open to a variant with a lower listing fee + higher marketing commit.

Please confirm what format procurement wants for modeling (your template vs. a memo). Also attaching the Q1 usage summary for your modeling. Looking to lock the commercial framework in the May 6 workshop.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive — Strategic Partners
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_ratecard_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet); redwood_aws_listing_playbook.pdf (PDF); usage_summary_Q1_2027.csv (CSV)
From: Alicia Chen <alicia.chen@amazon.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: aws-procurement@amazon.com, Matt Reynolds <matt.reynolds@cloudpath.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposed ratecard + playbook for May renewal workshop

Aditya — received, thanks for the clear proposal and attachments. I shared with procurement and partner ops. A couple quick notes:

- Procurement asked to see a one-page financial summary that shows effective take-rate at current + projected volumes (we can use your usage_summary CSV).
- Partner ops liked the placement guarantee ask — that helps surface you for co-sell.
- I've scheduled a 30-minute workshop for May 6, 10:00–10:30am PT. Invite sent to you, Laura, Marissa, and procurement.

Looping aws-procurement@amazon.com to start the official ratecard thread. We'll use the template you sent as the working doc.

Looking forward to the workshop.

Best,
Alicia Chen
Senior Partner Manager, AWS Marketplace
